title: Willie Mays's birth chart
metaDescription: Willie Mays's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 15.2° Taurus. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The chart's headline is a trine: Venus and Mars within 0.2°, taste wired to drive. A trine runs downhill — the talent that never announces itself because it never had to.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Measured rather than labelled, the Sun holds 15.2° Taurus: the second decan, whose classical sub-ruler is Mercury. An earth sign, read here in its second face.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 5.3° Taurus, Venus was at 12.7° Aries, Mars was at 12.9° Leo. Read together: a mind that trusts the measured and the checked; taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate; drive that ignites on contact.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Start where the chart is tightest — Venus trine Mars, 0.2° of separation. The scheme reads trines as water finding its level: effortless, and invisible to the person living it. Behind it, the Sun sextile Jupiter at 0.5°, and Jupiter square Uranus at 1.3° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The Moon opposes Jupiter while both square Venus. The t-square is the figure the old texts trusted for output: friction with a fixed address.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has four entries for this chart. The Moon in Capricorn at 12.8° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Venus in Aries at 12.7° is in detriment; Jupiter in Cancer at 15.7° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Saturn in Capricorn at 23.3° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Tallied where the signs are certain — 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day — the chart gives earth 5, fire 3, water 2, and cardinal 6, fixed 3, mutable 1 across the modes. Earth signs hold the scheme’s slow end, where results are measured in what survives rather than what starts. No settled placement falls in air — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Mercury, Saturn and Neptune were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Capricorn for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.9° between midnight and midnight. Fast enough that its degree is approximate, slow enough that its sign is not in doubt. At the noon reference it stands at 12.8°.
